The 1940–41 season was [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol's 38th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga|9th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
The club changed its president on 27 November 1940 with the arrival of Antonio Santos.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archivo.marca.com/centenario_realmadrid/presidentes/santosperalba.html|date=2 May 2002|accessdate=2 December 2020|title=Presidents: Antonio Santos Peralba|language=Spanish}}</ref> Also, on 1 January 1941 the club changed its name from Madrid Football Club back to Real Madrid Club de Futbol, recovering its honorific title that had been stripped by the [[Second Spanish Republic]] in 1931. In spite of the transfers in of Alday<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/blogs/ni-mas-ni-menos/archivo/2017/pagina/3/|title=Gonzalo Marza|publisher=marca.com|date=12 August 2017|accessdate=12 December 2020|author=Jesus Ramos|language=Spanish}}</ref> and Chus Alonso, the team collapsed to the 6th spot during the final rounds under the management of Paco Bru,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/blogs/ni-mas-ni-menos/2015/08/09/paco-bru-el-hombre-que-invento-la.html|title=The Man Who Invented The Spanish National Team|publisher=marca.com|date=9 August 2015|accessdate=9 December 2020|language=Spanish}}</ref> nine points below Champions Atletico Aviación.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/04/27/reportajes/1587991627_646125.html|title=Atlético Aviación Post Civil War|publisher=as.com|date=27 April 2020|accessdate=15 December 2020|language=Spanish}}</ref>
